issue.title: Custom gate with a failed command becomes unreachable: no gate-shell row registered, and a dismissed notification cannot be undismissed
issue.description:
A custom gate whose approved command **fails** can become unreachable from every UI, leaving `sase gate answer` on the CLI as the only way back in.

Found by phase agent `sase-13t.1.f1` while landing epic sase-13t (PyPI retention deletion gate `custom-fcaeb8b6`). The gate was still live and answerable (`acceptance.disposition=accepted_failed`, `can_supersede=true`) but invisible in both the gate list and the notification panel.

Two independent defects compound:

1. **No gate-shell row is registered.** The gate declared a full shell block in `request.json` (`PYPI-DELETE -> PYPI-DELETED`, `next.fork=family`), but `.creation_result.json` recorded `continuation_mode="none"`, and `sase gate list --all` returned 103 rows with this gate absent from all of them. So the shell block was accepted at request time and dropped at creation time.

2. **A dismissed gate notification cannot be recovered.** Both of the gate's notifications were dismissed (`428e38e5` the gate itself, `445f1135` the execution failure). `sase notify apply-state` offers dismiss / mute / read / snooze / unmute but has **no undismiss**, so dismissal is a one-way door. For contrast, the equivalent execution-failure notification for the earlier gate `custom-c1f4c258` (`b7f367d5`) was left undismissed and stayed reachable.

Net effect: an answerable gate that neither `sase gate list` nor the notification panel will show. The user's only routes are `sase gate answer <id>` from the CLI (if they still know the id) or creating a replacement gate.

Scope note: these are plausibly one fix or two. (1) is a gate-shell registration bug at the request -> creation seam; (2) is a missing notification action. Either alone leaves the gate reachable, which is why this is filed as one task rather than two.

task_type_fields.impact: A live, answerable gate is invisible in both the gate list and the notification panel. The user cannot reach it from any UI; recovery requires 'sase gate answer <id>' from the CLI with the id known in advance, or creating a replacement gate. In the reporting case this stalled an irreversible, human-gated PyPI deletion that only the maintainer could complete.
task_type_fields.location: sase gate creation (shell-block handling at the request -> .creation_result.json seam) and sase notify apply-state
task_type_fields.repro: Create a custom gate declaring a shell block whose approved command then fails (observed: gate custom-fcaeb8b6, 2026-09-20). Then: 1) 'sase gate list --all' does not list the gate although it is still answerable (acceptance.disposition=accepted_failed, can_supersede=true); .creation_result.json records continuation_mode="none" while request.json carries the shell block. 2) Dismiss its notifications, then try to get them back: 'sase notify apply-state' exposes dismiss/mute/read/snooze/unmute and no undismiss.

payload.description: sase-14g is the rowless-gate bug this guard hardens against

payload.entry: Both halves fixed and verified by the sase-14n.15 land agent at master 1567269ca. (1) Gate-shell row: sase gate create already routed shell requests through create_gate_shell, which registers the row. The rowless path was a direct create_gate call, which now fails with missing_gate_shell_row for shell-block custom specs (c6807d24c). An e2e test through create_gate_shell asserts continuation_mode gate_shell, the member row, and list_gate_shells / sase gate list --all visibility. Built-in kinds are follow-up sase-161. (2) Undismiss: sase notify apply-state undismiss (sase-14n.13) plus the ACE notification modal's T dismissed view and u restore (a8bd795be). A production-path test restores a dismissed live CustomGate and reaches handle_custom_gate from the normal inbox.
